Not shown: that AC3 is dominant or that it has 'no tail'. (1) Against AC2, it loses c31: per-launch 55.5-62.4 vs 47.5-52.8 us, worse in every round, and latency 22-33 vs 17-26 us. M100 pays 0.1-1.0 more cores and has bad tails under load (c01 3.5%, c15 6.6% over 1 ms). (3) Against AC, it loses c21 latency by about 4 us in every round and uses 0.002-0.013 more cores in every burst cell and round. (4) 'No tail' is overstated. AC3 has 6-8 calls over 1 ms per 4095 in c32 (max 5.4 ms). Over the whole run its per-launch mean is about 50 us above the median (121-128 vs 74.4-74.7), against 10-24 us for P, and that only equals ACn. The over-1-ms counts cover the first ~14% of the run; AC5 r4 has the fewest of them but the highest whole-run mean. Untested risks, read from the patch: the window closes only on two gaps of 50 us or more in a row, any caught or short gap resets the count, and otherwise the window never shrinks. With interleaved short and long gaps, the window never closes and polls up to 50 us after every request. Such patterns include two or more calls per launch on 50-300 us kernels, entry plus exit probes, or alternating 30/80 us gaps. At 55-115 us long gaps that approaches continuous polling, and c23 (every gap long) cannot reveal it. AC2 would reset to 0 after each long gap. In c31, AC3's state is set by the 20 us deferral quantum against the 50 us threshold (windows swing between 0 and 20 us and never reach a size that catches the ~30-45 us gaps). That depends on platform timing and could flip to AC5-like polling. The matrix also lacks multi-process, graph, partial or duty load, and any unseen-latch case.

It has not been tested on interleaved short/long gap patterns, where its two-in-a-row close rule never fires.

The noise floor between behaviourally identical sets is about 0.05 core: in c23, AC2/AC3/AC4/AC5/ACn all keep every window closed with 0 hot iterations, yet their CPU spans +0.03 to +0.14. c31 runs switch regime within a run, so its per-set ranges overlap widely (ACn per-launch 54-69 us).

The c31/c32 'CPU minus P' metric is negative for the sleeping sets (-0.03 to -0.18) because P's host thread uses 0.48-0.77 core and its share depends on latency. Use between-set differences, which match hot iterations at about 105-112 ns each, not absolutes or comparisons with P.
The c32 P baseline drifts monotonically across rounds (per-launch mean 37.9, 44.6, 49.8, 55.9 us; load rate 718k to 755k/s), so c32 'load vs P' is above 1.03 for every set in r1 and below 1 in r4.

Matrix limits: procs=1 and graph=0 in every cell, and only on6 full load (no on3 or duty6). unseen_latch=0 everywhere, so v2's latch rule (shared by AC2-ACn) was never exercised. Single platform at fixed clocks, one build.

The set descriptions in CLAIMS-v3 omit the late-sleep guard: when late_ewma exceeds 30 us, the 8 deferral sleeps are skipped and the watcher goes to 100 us slow sleeps or parks. Under load its use differs strongly by set (c05: AC2/AC4 about 4-4.6k skips per run vs 350-660 for AC/AC3/AC5) and it sets the size of the c05 regression. The descriptions also omit v1 AC's 1 ms episode cap.

Run order is shuffled per round and cell, and rounds5.log matches the seeded shuffle. No order effect is visible: AC3 and AC5 agree in bursts despite different positions. Time span 14:35-15:22; one build (agent .so built at 14:33 from the 14:32:58 source).

summarize.py validity ignores disturbance and mid-run clocks. 'Cost per call' divides per-launch overhead, including per-launch hook cost, by the lane count. M100 has no counters. The c23 header '55-115 us' describes P's gaps; bpftime's are about 10 us longer.

Patch nit: long_run is a signed int that increments without bound while the window is closed. It overflows (undefined behaviour) only after 2^31 consecutive long gaps, so it is harmless in practice. Correct as claimed: the first request after start counts as one long gap and leaves win at 0, and a caught or short gap resets the count.
